title: Choice independence of smooth density integration
statement: Let $N$ be a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth real $m$-manifold without boundary [def-sfb-smooth-real-manifold], and $\omega$ a smooth section [def-sfb-smooth-bundle-sections] of $\mathrm{Dens}_N$ [def-sfb-smooth-density-line]. For any two finite smooth chart covers $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ and smooth subordinate partitions of unity $\rho,\sigma$ as in [def-sfb-smooth-density-integral], the chart-sum integrals satisfy $J_{\mathcal A,\rho}(\omega)=J_{\mathcal B,\sigma}(\omega)$. Thus the integral is independent of all chart and partition choices. For each such fixed cover and partition, $\omega\mapsto J_{\mathcal A,\rho}(\omega)$ is a real-linear functional.

source.place: WANTED locally: inherited Part I §3.A–3.B, printed pp.11–13 (page attribution inherited, not independently verified). Agent-stated real density convention, supporting chart and partition independence needed to name the density integral. No claim of reading this unavailable source.

proof.text: First dispose of the small cases directly from the chart-sum definition. If $N=\varnothing$, every summand is zero. If $m=0$, each nonempty chart domain is one point, since $\mathbf R^0$ is a singleton. A finite chart cover therefore makes $N$ a finite set. The empty determinant is $1$, so every density fibre has the same canonical generator; write its coefficient at $p$ as $a(p)$. By [def-sfb-euclidean-lebesgue-integral], zero-dimensional Lebesgue measure is the empty product measure, of mass $1$ on its singleton; the integral of the constant simple function $c$ is consequently $c\cdot1=c$. Hence either chart sum is $\sum_{p\in N}a(p)\sum_{i:p\in U_i}\rho_i(p)=\sum_{p\in N}a(p)$. This is independent of the cover and partition and is real-linear, including when charts repeat. Below assume $m\geq1$.

source.place: Agent argument for the inherited analytic prerequisite; empty-space and dimension-zero cases from the definitions.

proof.text: Write the two chart families as $x_i:U_i\to V_i$ and $y_j:W_j\to Z_j$, and the density coefficients as $a_i$ and $b_j$. Use the closed-support convention explicitly specified by [def-sfb-smooth-density-integral]: $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i=\overline{\{p:\rho_i(p)\neq0\}}$. Let $K_i=\operatorname{supp}\rho_i\subset U_i$ and $L_j=\operatorname{supp}\sigma_j\subset W_j$. They are closed subsets of compact $N$, hence compact. In chart $x_i$, the coefficient of $\rho_i\omega$ is smooth and vanishes off the compact subset $x_i(K_i)\subset V_i$. Its extension by zero is continuous on $\mathbf R^m$: on $V_i$ it is already smooth; at any point outside $V_i$, the complement of the closed compact set $x_i(K_i)$ is a neighborhood on which the extension vanishes. The same argument applies to $\sigma_j\omega$, to $\rho_i\sigma_j\omega$ in either chart, and to finite partial sums of these localized densities. For a product the supporting compact set is $K_i\cap L_j\subset U_i\cap W_j$.

source.place: Agent argument for the inherited density-integration prerequisite: compact supports and zero extension.

proof.text: Every zero-extended coefficient in the previous step is integrable. Indeed, regard its continuous compactly supported real function $f$ as the complex-valued function $f+0\mathrm i$. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-compact-support-integrable] to this complex function on $\mathbf R^m$, using $m\geq1$, then [lem-sfb-complex-integral-real-projection] to its real part, which is $f$. This proves the integrability hypotheses needed for all finite-sum linearity applications below, including their partial sums.

For each $i,j$, set $D=x_i(U_i\cap W_j)$, $E=y_j(U_i\cap W_j)$ and $\phi=y_j\circ x_i^{-1}:D\to E$. These are open sets and a smooth diffeomorphism by the manifold definition. In the $x_i$ and $y_j$ generators let the coefficients of $\rho_i\sigma_j\omega$ be $f$ and $g$. The current density-line definition gives $g_{x_i y_j}(p)=|\det D\phi(x_i(p))|$ and coefficient transport $a\mapsto a/g_{x_i y_j}(p)$; equivalently, its density transition rule gives exactly $f(z)=|\det D\phi(z)|g(\phi(z))$. Apply [lem-sfb-euclidean-jacobian-integral] to $g+0\mathrm i$ on $E$. Use the inclusion identity of [lem-sfb-complex-integral-real-projection] for both restricted Lebesgue measures, and injectivity of $\mathbf R\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, to obtain $\int_D f=\int_E g$. Each coefficient vanishes outside the overlap in its larger chart. Thus its integral on the overlap is its full zero-extended integral: in both integrals it is the same function against Lebesgue measure, zero off the overlap. Denote these full chart integrals by $I_{x_i}(\rho_i\sigma_j\omega)$ and $I_{y_j}(\rho_i\sigma_j\omega)$. They are equal, also for an empty overlap.

source.place: integral_target_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul, lines 1225–1232; density coefficient convention from def-sfb-smooth-density-line.

proof.text: Pointwise $\rho_i\omega=\sum_j\rho_i\sigma_j\omega$ because $\sum_j\sigma_j=1$. Likewise $\sigma_j\omega=\sum_i\rho_i\sigma_j\omega$. In the fixed $x_i$ chart, apply real linearity from [lem-sfb-euclidean-bochner-integral-calculus] repeatedly to this finite sum; its terms and partial sums are integrable by steps 2–3. Here its target $\mathbf R^1$ is identified with $\mathbf R$, and its unused dimension parameter can be set to $1$. Do the same in each $y_j$ chart. Summing the equalities from step 4 and commuting finite sums gives $$J_{\mathcal A,\rho}(\omega)=\sum_i\sum_j I_{x_i}(\rho_i\sigma_j\omega)=\sum_j\sum_i I_{y_j}(\rho_i\sigma_j\omega)=J_{\mathcal B,\sigma}(\omega).$$ This compares arbitrary two choices directly, without choosing charts for a third atlas.

source.place: integral_add, lines 237–240, and integral_smul, lines 275–278; finite induction and partition identities are written out in this step.

proof.text: Fix one chart cover and partition. For smooth densities $\omega,\eta$ and real scalars $c,d$, pointwise vector-space operations on sections give chart coefficient $c a_i+d e_i$ for $c\omega+d\eta$, where $a_i,e_i$ are the coefficients of $\omega,\eta$. Multiplication by the fixed $\rho_i$ and extension by zero preserve this equality. Each localized coefficient is integrable by steps 2–3, so [lem-sfb-euclidean-bochner-integral-calculus] gives $I_{x_i}(\rho_i(c\omega+d\eta))=cI_{x_i}(\rho_i\omega)+dI_{x_i}(\rho_i\eta)$. Sum over the finite cover to obtain $J_{\mathcal A,\rho}(c\omega+d\eta)=cJ_{\mathcal A,\rho}(\omega)+dJ_{\mathcal A,\rho}(\eta)$. Together with step 1 this proves the asserted linearity in every dimension.
